new_defects.title: State index URL flipped: /en/state now 404, /en/states is now canonical
new_defects.evidence: On 2026-04-30, /en/state returned 200 (137KB index) and /en/states returned 308 → /en/state. Today the polarity has flipped: /en/state returns 404 (27,436 bytes), and /en/states returns 200 directly (137,804 bytes). The plural is now canonical. Region-side: /en/regions correctly redirects to /en/states (closing yesterday's NEW-2026-04-30-008), and all /en/region/<slug> URLs continue to 301 to /en/state/<slug>. The route map is consistent end-to-end, but any inbound links, sitemap entries, or external references to /en/state will now hit a 404 — and yesterday those URLs were live.
new_defects.impact: Yesterday's index URL (/en/state) was indexed by search engines as 200; today it serves a 404. Until Google re-crawls and accepts /en/states, the state-index page may temporarily show as 'soft 404' or drop in coverage. SEO equity should re-coalesce within a crawl cycle, but the singular→plural inversion within one day is unusual.
new_defects.recommended_owner: web (apps/web/src/app/[locale]/state*/page.tsx — confirm the flip is intentional, then add /en/state → 301 → /en/states to preserve crawl equity)

new_defects.title: Hindi month sub-route still ships an English-only <title>

But the month variant /hi/destination/jaipur/march still serves the English title 'Jaipur in March 2026: Great time (15–30°C) | NakshIQ'. Body content size (183,511 bytes) suggests real content rendered, but the page <title> + likely the rest of the chrome was not run through the same i18n pass that the destination root just received.
new_defects.impact: Hindi-search users see English titles in SERPs for month pages. Inconsistent with the destination-root improvement. Likely a one-line fix in the month-route page component.
new_defects.recommended_owner: web/i18n (apps/web/src/app/[locale]/destination/[slug]/[month]/page.tsx — same pattern as the slug page that got localized today)

new_defects.title: hreflang link tags now present in DOM but absent from server-rendered HTML
new_defects.evidence: On /en/destination/jaipur the live DOM contains 2 <link rel='alternate' hreflang> tags (en → /en/destination/jaipur, hi → /hi/destination/jaipur). But curl on the same URL returns 0 hreflang tags in the server-rendered HTML (verified on jaipur, leh, /en, /hi, /en/collections). This means hreflang is being injected by client-side JavaScript after hydration — Googlebot does run JS but most other crawlers (LLMs, Bing, social previews) do not, so the SEO signal only lands for a subset of consumers.
new_defects.impact: Partial close on the 5-day-old hreflang gap (NEW-2026-04-30-003). Googlebot will eventually pick up the alternates, but other crawlers won't. Recommend rendering hreflang in the SSR <head> via Next.js metadata API so the tag appears in the curl response too.
new_defects.reproduction:
curl -s https://www.nakshiq.com/en/destination/jaipur | grep -oE 'rel="alternate"[^>]*hreflang' | wc -l   # → 0
Then open the same URL in Chrome and run: document.querySelectorAll('link[rel="alternate"][hreflang]').length   # → 2

new_defects.title: /sitemap/5.xml route still resolves 200 with empty <urlset> after being removed from the index
new_defects.evidence: Today's /sitemap.xml index lists chunks 0..4 only — chunk 5 was removed from the index. But GET /sitemap/5.xml still returns 200 with 111 bytes (empty <urlset>). /sitemap/6.xml correctly returns 404. The empty chunk no longer wastes a guaranteed crawl slot, but the route is still reachable; cleaner to 404 it for parity with /sitemap/6.xml.
new_defects.impact: Cosmetic/cleanup — bots that previously cached chunk 5's 200 may keep refreshing it; a 404 is more honest.

new_defects.title: Soft-404 on /destination/<bad-slug> persists in BOTH locales (8th consecutive day)
new_defects.evidence: /en/destination/this-does-not-exist-xyz → 200, 73,683 bytes; /hi/destination/this-does-not-exist-xyz → 200, 84,263 bytes. new_defects.impact: Crawlers can index unbounded fake URLs; analytics gets dirtied; llms.txt 'destinations' list points at slugs that 200-but-don't-exist. 8 consecutive days flagged.
new_defects.recommended_owner: web (apps/web/src/app/[locale]/destination/[slug]/page.tsx — call notFound() when the row is missing)

new_defects.title: Numeric month sub-routes /destination/<slug>/<1-12> still soft-404 (llms.txt contract violation)
new_defects.evidence: Probed /en/destination/jaipur/3, /5, /10 and /en/destination/shimla/3, /5, /10 — all returned 200 with 73,833–73,835 bytes (homepage shell). new_defects.impact: AI crawlers following llms.txt advice get indexed onto homepage HTML for what they think are month-specific destination pages — bad for citation quality and llms.txt audits.
new_defects.recommended_owner: web (apps/web/src/app/[locale]/destination/[slug]/[month]/page.tsx — accept numeric and name forms, or add a 1..12 → name redirect)

new_defects.title: Confidence mention count drops EXACTLY 2 in /hi vs /en across all 11 destinations (8th day with same delta)
new_defects.evidence: Per-page count of literal token 'confidence' in HTML, en→hi: jaipur 11→9, shimla 12→10, manali 15→13, leh 13→11, varanasi 11→9, udaipur 9→7, darjeeling 9→7, kaza 8→6, panaji 10→8, munnar 9→7, binsar 8→6. Delta is consistently 2 — strongly suggests two specific 'confidence' UI strings remain English-only on /en pages while their /hi counterparts are localized to a different word (or absent). Identical to 2026-04-29..30 even though today's bigger i18n pass localized titles.
new_defects.impact: Adds a deterministic data point under BUG-005 — the gap is a fixed two-string bug, not rolling content drift. Today's title localization didn't touch it.
new_defects.reproduction: for s in jaipur shimla manali leh varanasi udaipur darjeeling kaza panaji munnar binsar; do for l in en hi; do curl -s https://www.nakshiq.com/$l/destination/$s | grep -oiE confidence | wc -l; done; done

gaps: deployment_id not captured this run — x-vercel-id rotates per request and I didn't grab a x-vercel-deployment-id from the response headers. Day-over-day deploy fingerprint comparison is approximate.

Cold-render performance is collected from whatever happens to be cache=MISS on probe; no controlled invalidation. Today's MISS set was darjeeling (en+hi) and binsar (en+hi) — same as 2026-04-30, so the cold-render comparison is reasonable.

Live console message capture is partial — Chrome MCP starts tracking only after the first read_console_messages call. BUG-012 verdict relies on a navigate-then-read pattern; only the chrome-extension messages were captured (9 entries), so any synchronous Supabase warnings emitted before navigation completed could be missed.

I did not enumerate /en/states' child link count or compare against /en/state's historical inventory — recommend a state-route inventory test for the next run, especially given today's singular→plural URL flip.

Browser-side hreflang is checked on jaipur and leh only — recommend extending to /hi pages and /en/collections to confirm the client-side injection covers all routes, not just the destination-root pattern.
